subject: Control plane sequestration and on-prem VPC reference handoff
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control plane sequestration: reference diagrams and next steps

Jordan / Acme infra team —

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Attached are the updated reference diagrams that implement the control-plane sequestration pattern we discussed. High-level summary:

- Control-plane components (operator API, key mgmt, rollout controller) sit inside an isolated management VPC and egress only to customer-approved CIDRs via a dedicated egress gateway.
- Data-plane inference nodes live in customer tenant subnets and communicate to the control plane via an authenticated, mTLS-protected relay over a pinned peering (no public IPs).
- KV cache replication is unidirectional (control -> node) to minimize sensitive metadata exposure; logs and traces are forwarded to your observability collector via a pull model.

Action items we need from Acme before we start the canary handoff:
1) Confirm allowed egress CIDR(s) for the control-plane gateway and the expected NAT translation behavior.
2) Confirm KMS/HSM provisioning plan and whether Redwood will use a customer-managed key.
3) Any MTU / BGP constraints on the colo side (MTU < 1500)?
We recommend a 1-week canary window; proposed start: 2028-04-10. Attached: vpc-reference-schematic-v2.pdf (diagram), canary-runbook.md (ops checklist).

If you want a short walkthrough, Jonas can run it with your infra team — I’ve cc’d him.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-reference-schematic-v2.pdf (diagram, 1.8MB), canary-runbook.md (markdown, 12KB)
From: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Control plane sequestration: reference diagrams and next steps

Vanessa —

Appreciate the diagrams. Quick clarifications from our side:

- On the egress CIDR: we can provide 3 contiguous /28s but they’re behind a NAT pool and SNAT is performed at the colo. Is that architecture compatible with the control-plane callback pattern you show?
- We prefer customer-managed KMS but need to ensure RFC-compliance for key rotation; any constraints on HSM vendor?
- Our colo runs BGP with MD5 on the session and enforces 1400 MTU for the tenant VLANs. Will that break the kept-alive KV replication?
Also, are you planning any sidecar (WireGuard / service mesh) on the inference nodes for egress protection or do you rely on the underlying host?
Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Li
SRE Lead, Acme Corp

On Tue, Mar 20, 2028 at 09:12 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane sequestration: reference diagrams and next steps

Jordan —

Short answers (tl;dr at top):
- SNAT at the colo is fine. Our control-plane callbacks are idempotent and rely on mTLS session origination from the control VPC; as long as the colo preserves source IP consistency within the pool for session affinity, we’re OK.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are supported. We integrate with common HSM vendors via an external key provider interface. Rotation is automated but we will need an initial key import window (we document the exact steps in the drive link).
- MTU=1400: that’s workable. We shard/fragment large protobuf blobs at the application layer; you may want to increase TCP MSS if possible but we won’t require MTU changes for the pilot.
About sidecars:
- The pattern we shipped in the diagrams is host-based TLS (mTLS from process to control relay). We recommend an optional WireGuard sidecar if you want kernel-level isolation + static routing; it’s a drop-in but not strictly required for the first canary.
I’ve added a short note to INF-7034 with the MTU/BGP acceptance criteria (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-7034). Vanessa — I attached the slightly annotated canvas to the ticket and flagged the egress CIDRs.
Next steps:
- Jordan: please confirm the exact /28s and the SNAT mapping behavior (static translation vs ephemeral pool) by 2028-03-25.
- Acme security: confirm HSM vendor (we’ll provide import template).
Happy to demo the traffic flow if useful — can do a 30-min session next week.

—Jonas
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference

> On Wed, Mar 21, 2028 at 10:04 AM Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme.com> wrote:
> > Vanessa —
> > 
> > Appreciate the diagrams. Quick clarifications from our side...
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control plane sequestration: reference diagrams and next steps — canary signoff request

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick confirmations in the thread. Per Jonas’ notes: SNAT behind a stable pool is OK and MTU=1400 is supported with our fragmentation guardrails. We’ll plan the canary as discussed.

Deliverables we’ll provide before the cutover (by 2028-04-03):
- Finalized diagram set (including BGP session detail) — vpc-reference-schematic-v2.pdf (attached).
- Canary runbook with rollback criteria and observability dashboards — canary-runbook.md (attached).
- KMS import template and HSM integration checklist (link in INF-7034).

Please sign off on the three items above by 2028-03-25 so we can hold the 2028-04-10 canary start. If Acme wants the WireGuard sidecar enabled for the pilot, we can add it to the runbook but that will add a single-day ops window for image rollout.

If everything’s good I’ll schedule a 30-min pre-cutover dry run with Acme SRE + our Ops on 2028-04-05.
Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-reference-schematic-v2.pdf, canary-runbook.md
